annotations.title: EU article as of a date

description: POINT-IN-TIME for EU law: what an article of a regulation or directive SAID on a given date, not what it says today. The EU twin of lookup_article_at_date. Consolidated versions are collapsed by text, so an article consolidated thirty times with two actual wordings reports two versions rather than thirty — you see when the text really changed. Omit `date` to get the version in force now plus the list of versions. USE THIS whenever the question is about a past moment: a transaction, a deadline, a rate as it stood in some year. Reports honestly when no consolidated version covers the date rather than handing back the earliest text, which would claim a provision applied before it existed.

date.description: The date, YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for the version in force today.

name: lookup_eu_article_at_date
